consentRecord.whyChannelIsClosed: Closing the answer channel to the controlling terminal removes the PIPE vector, and that is the whole of what it removes. A here-document, a script's stdout, a CI wrapper's stdin or any redirected file cannot supply the token, because the token is not read from stdin at all. ConsentRecordV1 records answerChannel so that a persisted policy carries the channel its consent arrived on.
consentRecord.whatTheChannelDoesNotClose: It does not close the pseudo-terminal vector. A harness that allocates a pseudo-terminal -- script, expect, unbuffer, docker -t -- presents a controlling terminal that satisfies every terminal test a process can perform, and can type the token. No software distinguishes a human at a terminal from a program driving one. v23 claimed this control defeated 'the same automation the CI rule exists to keep out'; it does not, and the predecessor's review was right to call that an overclaim. What actually keeps automation out is the invocationProfile classification below, which is one-directional: a terminal never PROMOTES an invocation to local-interactive. The residual that survives even that is RT24-A-RES-06.

disclosure.text:
OpenSIP has no storage and retention policy for this project.

Evidence derived from your source code can be kept on this machine so that a later run can verify or replay this one, or it can be discarded when this run ends.

Keeping it writes files derived from your source code under this project's OpenSIP storage directory. Discarding it means a later run cannot verify or replay this one; the record that the run happened is kept either way.

You can change this later, and you can purge what has been kept. Purging removes the stored evidence and reduces what a later run can do with it; it does not rewrite or delete the sealed record that the run happened. OpenSIP cannot remove copies outside its own storage directory - filesystem journals, remapped media, swap, or your own backup and sync copies.

Keep evidence for this project? Type yes or no:

noAskCases.name: CI and every other non-interactive invocation
noAskCases.decision: CI never prompts, never writes a policy and never infers one. It is read-only with respect to the policy. With no policy present, an ephemeral or advisory request proceeds ephemeral and a durable-authoritative request is refused at request-validation.
noAskCases.consistencyWithA1RI04: A1-RI-04 decided CI_IGNORES_LAYER_4 and gave the reason: an unreviewed local file must not change CI, but mere file presence must not become a CI denial-of-service switch. Part A keeps both halves. Policy absence is not an admission failure on the ephemeral path, so no CI job breaks because a policy was never answered on somebody's laptop. Policy absence is a refusal on the durable-authoritative path only, which is the one path where proceeding would mean choosing a retention default. Reading an already-persisted policy is not resolving layer 4: the policy is host-owned project state, not a configuration layer, and it never enters PlanId.
noAskCases.whyNotSimplyProceedEphemeral: A durable-authoritative request that silently produced ephemeral evidence would be a durability failure reporting authoritative success, which freeze law 14 forbids, and a silent demotion of a sealed capability target, which evidence.v10 sealedCapabilityContract.finalization forbids.

noAskCases.choice: REFUSE-TO-START-UNTIL-ANSWERED, with the ask relocated to request-validation

rejectedAlternatives.option: buffer the in-flight evidence pending an answer
rejectedAlternatives.rejectedBecause: Buffering means user-derived evidence exists in host memory with no policy governing its custody, which is precisely the state v22's recommendedDefaultPosture forbids. It is also not honestly reversible: a buffer large enough to matter reaches swap and the page cache, and freeze section 7 records that DeletionProtocol cannot erase swap. A 'no' answer would then have to be honoured by a deletion the tool cannot perform.

rejectedAlternatives.option: discard the in-flight run and re-run after the answer
rejectedAlternatives.rejectedBecause: It doubles the work, and worse it makes a partial execution that produced real derived data unrecorded. An unrecorded partial execution is the standing invitation to keep its results 'just this once'.

noAskCases.whyRelocatingIsTheRepair: The premise that evidence exists in memory while the question is open is created by asking too late. C-2 v4's admission boundary places request-validation strictly before attempt-admission and snapshot capture strictly after admission. Asking at request-validation means that at ask time there is no ExecutionId, no AttemptRecord, no SnapshotId, no PlanId, no ExecutionPlan and no Run. There is nothing to buffer and nothing to discard.
noAskCases.consequenceForExecutionId: None is allocated. Freeze law 6 allocates ExecutionId at attempt admission, which is after the ask in every branch. If the user answers, request-validation completes and admission proceeds normally, allocating exactly one ExecutionId. If the user dismisses, request-validation terminates and no ExecutionId is allocated. No retention answer ever arrives after ExecutionId allocation.
noAskCases.consequenceForAttemptRecord: None is created. AttemptRecord is allocated with ExecutionId at attempt admission, so the admitted PlanIntent it stores is never written twice and never written under an undetermined custody policy.
noAskCases.theAskIsNotAnalysis: Freeze law 5: the orchestration host performs effects and the core receives sealed data with no effectful callback or port. The ask is a host effect at request-validation. The core never sees the policy, never sees the prompt and cannot trigger one.

outcomes.trigger: bounded reprompt count exhausted without a token in the closed answer set

noAskCases.nonTtyStdoutAndPipedStdin: Neither is a dismissal state. Both are inputs to the profile classification made before an ask can exist, and both point in one direction only: a non-TTY stdout or a stdin that is not a terminal FORCES profile ci, and the invocation falls to case 1 where nothing is ever asked. The converse does not hold. A controlling terminal does not promote an invocation to local-interactive, because a pseudo-terminal satisfies every terminal test a process can perform. Separately, ConsentRecordV1 closes answerChannel to the controlling terminal, so a pipe cannot supply an answer even if one were solicited -- which removes the pipe vector and, as consentRecord.whatTheChannelDoesNotClose records, nothing beyond it.
noAskCases.sigintExitCodeIsDerivedNotChosen: The pinned D9 v1.14 reference derivation returns request-rejected at exit 2 for a signal arriving while admission is rejected, because D9 reclassifies a signal only while the outcome is still unsettled and a rejected request is settled. Exit 130 requires admission=admitted, which is false before attempt admission. This artifact reports the derived value rather than the value it would have preferred, and records the consequence as residual RT23-A-RES-03.

closureMeasurement.question: At which positions of the PLAN-ID-V1 preimage can a host place the persisted retention policy's posture or identity without PLAN-ID-V1 refusing?
closureMeasurement.whyMeasuredAndNotEnumerated: This corpus has now replaced five enumerations with measurements for exactly one reason: an enumeration is complete only if its author thought of everything, and the author never does. Section 8's escalation list, the C-2 residual table, the C-2 type-space walk and the C-2 pin population went first. This is the fifth.
method: Read PLAN-ID-V1's machine-checkable rules from the live pinned contract: the closed key lists, the enums, the regexes, the constants, the sort and uniqueness rules, the budget key pattern and the declared input classes.

Anchor the resulting admission both ways: it must reproduce the pinned positive golden planid-v1-ci-minimal exactly, and it must return the declared violation code for every negative golden expressible as a descriptor mutation.

Build a probe descriptor that instantiates ONE occurrence of every structure the contract declares -- the anchor golden supplies the base, the full-providers golden supplies both semantic universes, nestedClosure supplies the capability grants. The admission must ADMIT it; if the probe base were refused, no refusal below would carry information.
WALK the probe. Every map, every array of strings and every string slot is a position, enumerated by the walk rather than by an author.

At each position attempt to place the policy in every rendering it actually has: the posture token, the RETENTION-POLICY-ID-V1 text, that identity's bare 64-hex digest, and the posture as an unsigned integer. A position ADMITS if any rendering survives.
Publish the counts and the admitting positions as the OUTPUT of that run. The instrument recomputes all of it on every execution and refuses any published list that has drifted from what it measured.
closureMeasurement.probeDescriptorIsNotAGolden: The probe is constructed by this checker, not published by the contract. That is stated plainly because it is the one authored choice in the measurement: 'one occurrence of every declared structure'. Its PlanId is published so the construction is reproducible, and the walk over it is mechanical.
closureMeasurement.whatTheZeroMeans: Not one admitted position leaves the PlanId unchanged. Every position at which the policy can be placed is a position at which it CHANGES the PlanId, which is exactly the determinism break the constraint forbids: identical code producing different PlanIds depending on a UX answer.

familyMeanings.key-injection: add a NEW KEY to a map inside the preimage. This is the family the predecessor's blocking finding names: a ninth position, capabilityGrants[].parameters, is a key injection.
familyMeanings.array-element-injection: append a NEW ELEMENT to a declared array of strings, respecting whatever sort and uniqueness rule governs it.
familyMeanings.value-substitution: write the policy into a slot the contract already declares. PLAN-ID-V1 constrains the SHAPE of the preimage; with a handful of regex, enum and constant exceptions it does not constrain what a declared slot may say.

closureMeasurement.whyTheTwoSidedControlMatters: The predecessor's independent review computed these two PlanIds with its own PLAN-ID-V1 implementation, written from the contract's prose and never from an instrument of ours. Both grants are admitted and they differ, so the POLICY VALUE ALONE moves the PlanId at the position v23 did not enumerate. Reproducing them here byte for byte means the finding's evidence lives in the instrument rather than only in the review that raised it, and a future edit that quietly closed the position would break this control rather than pass unnoticed.
closureMeasurement.whatTheOpenSubStructuresAre: Every open sub-structure in the preimage -- that is the honest answer, and it is not two. A sub-structure is open when the contract closes the map that CONTAINS it but enumerates no member set for the map ITSELF. contributions[].parameters is open to a contribution's own verified schema. capabilityGrants[].parameters is open the same way and is the position v23 missed. budgets is open under a key PATTERN, which constrains spelling and not membership. compilerOptions is called 'the closed resolution/type-affecting subset keyed by option name' and no member set is enumerated anywhere in these bytes, so nothing reading them can refuse a key. standardLibraryComponentDigests closes its VALUES to 64 lowercase hex and its keys not at all -- and a RETENTION-POLICY-ID-V1 is a sha256, so its bare digest is a conforming value.
closureMeasurement.indexNormalisation: Positions are reported at both granularities: positionsProbed and positionsAdmitted count concrete positions in the probe, and admittingShapes collapses array indices to [*] so that three contributions do not read as three separate discoveries.
whatThisMeasurementDoesNotSettle: Whether each admitting position is closed in SUBSTANCE by a join this instrument cannot evaluate -- to a verified ReleaseManifest, to a contribution's own schema, to a C-2 stage or grant registry, to the sealed Snapshot, or to the AttemptRecord's frozen AdmissionDescriptor. Several plainly are. This artifact does not adjudicate them one by one, and says so rather than implying the admitting set is the exposed set.

The AdmissionDescriptor join is worth naming precisely, because it is the strongest of them and it still does not close this: planDescriptorSchema.admissionDescriptorEquality binds nine of the thirteen fields to the frozen descriptor stored in the AttemptRecord, and the contract's own negative goldens show post-admission substitution of contributions[].parameters, of a grant version and of an artifact digest each failing with PLAN_INTENT_COMMITMENT_MISMATCH. That closes SUBSTITUTION AFTER ADMISSION. It does not close INCLUSION AT ADMISSION: if the host wires the policy into the descriptor before it is frozen, the commitment covers the policy and there is no mismatch to detect. Which is precisely why the exclusion is a host wiring rule.

Positions inside structures the live contract forbids in the probe's configuration. The probe sets executionCapableResolution true so that buildScriptOutputs and procMacroOutputs are populated and their positions are reachable; a probe with it false would not reach them at all.

Appending a whole additional well-formed element to an array of OBJECTS -- another contribution, another grant, another stage. That vector reduces to the open sub-structure inside the new element, which is measured, but the element-level vector itself is not separately probed.

obligation.verbatim: State how purge changes current evidence availability without rewriting the sealed Run
obligation.priorState: Measured NOT DISCHARGED by the V10 disposition lane: the property is stated in several places and every place that states it fails a different gate. distinction.sealedCapability: IMMUTABLE. Frozen at request validation, committed in the admitted PlanIntent, and carried in the sealed SemanticCapabilityClosureV3. No availability event can change it.
distinction.effectiveCapability: DERIVED AT READ TIME from the sealed capability plus the current availability state. Never persisted into the sealed Run and never an input to any sealed identity.
distinction.terminalLoss: APPEND-ONLY. Recorded by appending to UnitAvailabilityLedgerV1. A terminal state is never reversed and no entry is ever edited or removed.
distinction.authority: WITHDRAWN BELOW VERIFIABLE. authoritative is derived as rank(effectiveCapability) >= rank(verifiable). Withdrawal is a read-time derivation returning false, not a rewrite of RunAuthorityIndexV1.
distinction.structuralBasis: v22's UNIT-ID-V3 preimage excludes objectStates and effectiveCapability, and SemanticCapabilityClosureV3 forbids objectStates, unitAvailabilityRecords and effectiveCapability outright. The mutable side therefore cannot enter the sealed bytes even by accident. This artifact recomputes both unitIds from that grammar rather than citing it.

meanings.AVAILABLE: present in this project's CAS and rehashes to its RawObjectKeyV1 digest
meanings.OUTAGE: transient: the store is reachable in principle but the object cannot be read now; reversible
meanings.MISSING-DEPENDENCY: absent from this project's CAS with no terminal-loss entry; reversible by restoring identical bytes, which is well defined because the key is the digest
meanings.PURGED: removed by an authorized retention action inside the tool's protection domain; terminal

availabilityStateLattice.whyThatPrecedence: A caller can act on an outage by retrying and on a missing dependency by restoring. A caller cannot act on a purge. Reporting the unactionable cause first stops a caller being told to retry something that will never come back. This mirrors D9's own precedence rule, which orders causes by how far trust has degraded rather than by severity.

ledger.sequenceRule: atSequence is strictly increasing by exactly one; a break is refused
ledger.foldRule: the current state of a raw key is the toState of its last entry
ledger.terminalRule: once a raw key carries a PURGED entry, any later entry for that key with toState != PURGED is refused
ledger.whyAppendOnly: This is what makes purge honest. The record of the loss is itself durable, so a purge cannot be undone by editing history, cannot be hidden, and cannot be made to look as though the Run never had the evidence. The seal says what was sealed; the ledger says what has since been lost; neither rewrites the other.
ledger.projectScope: one ProjectId per ledger, matching freeze law 8; a purge in one project never reaches an identical digest in another

inputs.name: availabilityRecords
inputs.source: fold of UnitAvailabilityLedgerV1 at read time

algorithm: A := { unitId -> { RawObjectKeyV1 -> state } } built from availabilityRecords.
unit_satisfied(u) := u.objectRefs is non-empty AND keys(A[u.unitId]) equals exactly { rawKey(r) for r in u.objectRefs } AND every state in A[u.unitId] is AVAILABLE.
satisfied(c) := unit_satisfied(u) for every unit u with rank(u.requiredForCapability) <= rank(c).
result := max { c in Capability : rank(c) <= rank(sealedCapability) and satisfied(c) }, and 'recorded' when that set is empty.

derivedProperties.statement: result is always at least 'recorded'; no availability state can remove the sealed record, because the seal is not an availability-controlled object
satisfied() is downward closed in rank, so the maximum is well defined and a single scan is exact
the derivation reads no field of the sealed Run other than sealedCapability and units, and writes nothing at all

PURGED, OUTAGE and MISSING-DEPENDENCY at the same position yield the same capability; the capability answers what can be produced now, and the cause is carried separately in currentAvailability and typedRefusal

The cause is what a person needs and it is carried where a person looks. It is also why the D9 reason-code gap below is a real cost rather than a cosmetic one: the class follows from the capability, and the code needs the cause.

Part B's stay at RT23-B- and the shared finding namespace stays at RT23- because Part B's counterexample rows NAME those ids and Part B is carried byte for byte. The mixed namespace is the visible cost of a byte-identical carry, and paying it is cheaper than editing a reviewed surface.
separability.sharedBaseAdjudication: Three shared-base checks run in BOTH modes by design: the recorded-input table, the residual measurement ledger and the Part B carry. A consequence, measured rather than assumed: editing Part B produces findings under --part a as well as --part b, because breaking the carry is a fact about the inheritance record and not a Part A semantic claim. Every finding it produces names $.partB_purgeSemantics or $.inheritance.partBCarriedFromPredecessorCandidate; none names a Part A path. The converse direction is the one the predecessor's review flagged: a Part A residual defect still surfaces under --part b through the shared residual recomputation, and it likewise names Part A paths only. Neither is a semantic dependency, and rejecting one part still does not require rejecting the other.
